boundary_decision.status: accepted as an authority-qualified vulnerability record aggregate
boundary_decision.rationale: The record owns vulnerability identity, attributable content containers, descriptions, affected-product assertions, assessments and disclosure history. Weakness classes, products, packages, deployed exposures, advisories, fixes, exploits, threats, incidents and risk decisions retain external identity and lifecycle.

decisions.rationale: CWE describes recurring weakness classes; a vulnerability record describes one source-qualified flaw or issue and may map to several classes.
CNA, ADP, NVD, vendor and ecosystem claims can coexist and must not silently overwrite each other.
A product-range assertion does not prove that a particular deployed asset contains, reaches or exposes the vulnerable configuration.
Same-vulnerability criteria are stricter than shared code, advisory grouping or conceptual similarity.
CVSS severity, EPSS probability, KEV inclusion, SSVC decisions and organizational risk answer different questions and vary by source and time.
Reservation, discovery, reporting, validation, vendor notice, embargo, disclosure, publication and knowledge are not one date or state.
A fixed version or workaround is not the same as patch deployment, exposure closure, incident response or risk acceptance.
Rejection, withdrawal, correction, split, merge and supersession preserve identifiers, references and cited predecessor evidence.
CVE, NVD, OSV, CSAF/VEX, STIX, CWE and CVSS overlap but have different authority and semantics.
Agents may maintain and validate records but cannot generate exploit instructions, scan without authority, break embargoes or disclose restricted evidence.
